translations.text: Paul and Silvanus and Timothy, to the churches of the Thessalonians, from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ:
Grace to you and peace from God the Father and our Lord Jesus Christ.
We ought always to give thanks to God for you, brothers, as is fitting, because your faith is growing all the more and the love of each one of you for one another is increasing,
so that we ourselves boast of you in the churches of God, because of your patience and faith in all your persecutions and afflictions that you endure,
as a sign of the righteous judgment of God, so that you may be made worthy of the kingdom of God, for which you are also suffering.
If indeed it is just for God to repay with affliction those who afflict you,
and to give you who are afflicted relief along with us at the revelation of our Lord Jesus Christ from heaven with the angels of his power,
to repay vengeance with flaming fire on those who do not know God and who do not obey the gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ,
on whom judgment will be brought, an eternal destruction, away from the face of the Lord and from the glory of his power,
when he comes to be glorified among his saints and to be marveled at among all his believers, because our testimony to you was found trustworthy, on that day.
For this reason we pray always for you, that God may make you worthy of the calling and fill you with every virtue of goodness, with the work of faith and with power,
so that the name of our Lord Jesus Christ may be glorified among you, and you through him, by the grace of our God and of our Lord Jesus Christ.
Now I say to you, brothers, concerning the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ and our gathering to him,
that you not be quickly shaken in mind or troubled, neither by spirit, nor by word, nor by letter, as if from us, as though the day of the Lord had arrived.
Let no one deceive you in any way, for unless the apostasy comes first, and the man of lawlessness is revealed, the son of perdition,
the one who attacks and exalts himself above all that are called god or object of worship, so that he even sits in the temple of God and displays himself as God.
Do you not remember that while I was still with you I told you this very thing?
And now, as you have been taught, you know what is to be revealed at its own proper time.
For the mystery of lawlessness is already at work, except only that the one who now holds it holds on until he goes far away,
and then that lawlessness will be revealed, which the Lord will wipe out with the breath of his mouth and bring to nothing by the manifestation of his coming,
whose coming is with the aid of the devil, with all power and signs and wonders of falsehood,
and with every deception of untruth among those who are perishing, since they did not accept the love of the truth so that they might be saved.
For this reason God will send them a helper of deception, so that they may believe the falsehood,
so that all may be judged who did not believe the truth but took pleasure in untruth.

But we ought to give thanks to God always for you, beloved brothers, by the Lord, because God chose you from the first as firstfruits of salvation, through the sanctification of the Spirit and faith in the truth,
to which he also called you through our gospel, for the obtaining of the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ.
From now on, brothers, stand firm and keep this teaching which you have learned, whether by word or by our letter.
And may our Lord Jesus Christ himself, and God our Father, who loved us and gave us eternal comfort and good hope through grace,
May he comfort your hearts and strengthen you in every good word and deed.
From now on, brothers, pray for us, that the word of God may run and be glorified, just as it is among you,
and that we may be delivered from disorderly and wicked men, for faith does not belong to all.
But the Lord is faithful, who will make you firm and guard you from evil.
And we trust in the Lord concerning you, that what we command you, you are both doing and will do.
And may the Lord direct your hearts to the love of God and the patience of Christ. 5
I command you, brothers, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that you keep away from every brother who walks in a disorderly way and not according to the teaching which he learned from us.
For you yourselves know how you ought to imitate us; for we did nothing improper among you;
nor did we eat bread from anyone without paying for it, but with toil and labor we worked night and day, so that we might not be a burden to any of you,
not because we do not have the authority, but in order to give ourselves to you as a model, so that you might imitate us.
For indeed, when I was with you, we commanded you this very thing: if anyone does not want to work, let him not eat either.
For I hear about some who conduct themselves among you in a disorderly way: they do no work, but go around as busybodies.
Such people, then, we command and entreat through our Lord Jesus Christ, that they work in quietness and eat their own bread.
But you, brothers, do not grow weary of doing good.
And if anyone does not obey our word through this letter, take note of him and do not associate with him, so that he may be ashamed.
Yet do not regard him as an enemy, but instruct him as a brother.
Now may the God of peace himself give you peace always in every way. The Lord be with you all!
The greeting is by my own hand, the hand of Paul, which is the sign in every letter; thus I have written:
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.
